claims.text: Feelings of loneliness had a higher negative impact on adolescents' happiness during COVID-19 quarantine than feelings of anxiety.
Anxious participants indicated using social media more often to actively seek ways to adapt to the situation.
Anxious participants used social media to a lesser extent as a way to keep in touch with friends and family.
The indirect effect of anxiety on happiness through active social media coping was significantly positive.
Participants feeling lonely were more inclined to use social media to cope with lacking social contact.
Using social media to cope with lacking social contact was not significantly related to feelings of happiness.
Humorous social media coping was positively related to feelings of happiness.
Humorous social media coping was not influenced by feelings of loneliness or anxiety.
Social media can serve as a constructive coping strategy for adolescents dealing with anxious feelings during quarantine.

evidence.description: Structural equation modeling revealed that feelings of loneliness had a higher negative impact on adolescents' happiness than feelings of anxiety.
Anxious participants indicated to use social media more often to actively seek for a manner to adapt to the current situation.
Anxious participants indicated using social media to a lesser extent as a way to keep in touch with friends and family.
The indirect effect of anxiety on happiness through active coping was significantly positive.
Participants who were feeling lonely were more inclined to use social media to cope with lacking social contact.
Coping with lacking social contact through social media was not significantly related to their happiness feelings.
Humorous coping was positively related with feelings of happiness.
Humorous coping was not influenced by loneliness or anxiety.
Social media can be used as a constructive coping strategy for adolescents to deal with anxious feelings during the COVID-19 quarantine.

methodologies.name: Structural Equation Modeling of Cross-Sectional Survey Data
methodologies.description: Evaluated relationships between anxiety, loneliness, happiness, and social media coping strategies using structural equation modeling.
datasets: Survey of 2,165 Belgian adolescents (13-19 years old)
